title: Sort Household Waste into Lidded Bins and Close Them
instruction: Sort the empty plastic drinks bottle, empty metal soup can, and food-stained paper napkin. Put the bottle and can in the green MIXED RECYCLING bin and the used napkin in the black GENERAL WASTE bin. Open each lid to put items in, then leave both lids closed. Do not put anything in the wrong bin.
context: Clearing a household snack table involves both sorting waste and operating the bins: open and hold a hinged lid, place the appropriate waste inside without trapping it at the rim, then close the lid. This task uses an explicitly stated household sorting policy; the green and black colours are not claimed to be universal. The used napkin must stay out of the mixed recyclables. A wrong-bin entry remains a failure even if the item is later recovered.
setup: Fixed YAM station with its two parallel-gripper arms, overhead and wrist RGB cameras (320 x 176), object_jitter=0, top_cam=demo, seed 42. Coordinates in metres: +x forward from the arm-base midpoint, +y left, z up; tabletop z=0.7475. Two rigid plastic round tabletop bins, outer diameter 0.172, inner diameter 0.164, height 0.190, floor thickness 0.008, mass 0.320 kg each, are fixed to the table at (0.200,-0.130) for green MIXED RECYCLING and (0.200,0.130) for black GENERAL WASTE. Each initially closed plastic lid is 0.180 m in diameter, 0.011 m thick and 0.046 kg, with a passive rear hinge limited to 110 degrees. The hinge is 0.081 m forward of the bin centre at z=0.9435. Each lid has a molded 0.025 x 0.030 x 0.052 m pinch post at local (-0.050,-0.055,0.026) on green or (-0.050,0,0.026) on black. Bin sides and lids carry white category lettering. The capped empty PET drinks bottle starts upright at (0.055,-0.015), height 0.140 m, body diameter about 0.052 m including trim, grasp waist diameter 0.036 m, mass 0.034 kg. The empty metal soup-can surrogate starts at (0,0.135), using the Arena tomato_soup_can library mesh scaled to longest extent 0.060 m (approximately 0.044 x 0.060 x 0.045 m), mass 0.040 kg. A folded food-stained paper-napkin surrogate starts at (-0.005,0.055), footprint approximately 0.060 x 0.046 m, thickness 0.011 m, mass 0.012 kg. Bottle and napkin are compound rigid primitives; the can uses a convex collision hull. Initial objects settle under gravity. Geometry and contact parameters are specified in assets.py and partkit.py.
scoring: End score in [0,1]. Any item entering the wrong bin latches score 0 for the rest of the episode. Entry means its entire horizontal projection is within the cavity and its bottom is at least 10 mm below the rim: bottle circular-shell samples use radius 83 mm from the bin centre; can and napkin AABB corners use radius 79 mm. Otherwise +0.25 per item fully contained, released and settled in its correct bin for 20 consecutive control steps (1 s), provided that bin has been robot-opened. Settled means top at least 2 mm below the rim, bottom at least 6 mm above the tabletop (3 mm for the can to accommodate visual-mesh/contact-hull mismatch), linear speed below 30 mm/s and angular speed below 0.35 rad/s. Released means each gripper is open above 70% or its TCP is more than 110 mm from the item origin. A bin is robot-opened when its lid reaches at least 60 degrees while increasing by more than 0.002 rad in a control step, with a gripper under 80% open and its TCP within 150 mm of the lid origin. Each opened bin containing at least one correctly settled item adds 0.10. Once all three items are correctly settled, both lids at or below 20 degrees add the final 0.05. Full score 1.0 ends the official trial. Opening lids alone gives 0; correctly filled but open bins give 0.95; unfinished or unsettled items receive no item credit. No prescribed item or bin order. State is checked at 20 Hz; exact predicates are in task.py.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 seconds of simulation).
reset_notes: Reset restores the fixed scene, closed lids, initial object positions, arms and score history. No consumables.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX contacts and passive revolute lid joints; unmodified YAM arms and cameras. Bins are fixed to the table. PET and stained paper are rigid surrogates, with no crushing, folding, liquid or contamination simulation. The can reuses an Arena mesh and convex hull. Masses and friction are representative, not hardware-calibrated. Scoring samples at 20 Hz and does not prove continuous collision avoidance.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (one official Inspect Robots trial, seed 42, 2,400 steps, max_steps, no runtime error); scripted physical demo: 1.0 (2,356 steps, success).
